lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hey Tamika, Pierre here. How's your Monday going?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, yes, perfect timing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Great. So today I'd like to hear how the walks after dinner went, check how you're feeling, and pick a goal for next week. Anything you want to add?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sounds good to me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Any problems this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So-so. Up and down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So did you manage to take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 5 days?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, only 4 days. It rained almost every afternoon.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's real progress.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I put a reminder on the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, no, not really. I kept saying tomorrow, tomorrow.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That sounds like an excuse to me.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm doing the best I can.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to make this a priority.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I know, I know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you wants this, and part of you is just worn out.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I already told my family about my goal.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to be around and be well for the people you love.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need this for my head too, not just my body.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What's worked for you before?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know, honestly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it. My neighbor started doing it with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I want to get my energy back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If you don't do this, your health is going to suffer.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Everybody keeps telling me that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You really shouldn't be drinking at all after cancer.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you mind if I tell you what some people do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Having a glass of water between drinks is an easy way to slow down.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll try to keep it to 2 drinks on the weekend.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If it rains I'll walk in the hallway of my building.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So, to sum up: the rain made this week harder, you still got 4 days in, and your plan is to keep it to 2 drinks on the weekend. Sound right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That's it exactly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Monday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Take care, Tamika. You're doing great.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, talk soon.

tags.note: Taking a concrete step with fridge reminder
Labels participant's reason as an excuse
Commits to this week, neighbor support
Warning about health right after change talk
Absolute directive on drinking, no permission
Expresses reason and need to act
Plans a backup for rainy days

flags.reason: Labels participant's struggle as an excuse, provoking defensiveness (line 16).
Directive 'You have to' without permission; participant responds with resignation.
Participant states wanting energy back; coach immediately moved to a warning instead of exploring it.
Absolute 'shouldn't be drinking at all' lecture; asked permission only for a later, softer suggestion.
Fear-based warning about health outcome; repeats pattern of persuading over exploring.

strengths: Line 10 affirms the 4 walking days despite rain, reinforcing effort.
Line 19 and 22 use complex reflections that capture ambivalence and family motivation well.
Line 43 and 46 use open questions to set the goal and plan for barriers, with the participant choosing a 2-drink goal.
coaching_tips: Line 15 and 17: replace 'That sounds like an excuse' and 'You have to' with an open question about what got in the way, e.g. 'What made tomorrow easier to say?'
Line 34 and 36: after the participant's change talk at line 33, reflect the energy goal instead of warning; ask permission before giving health information.
Line 41: 'I don't want the cancer back' is strong change talk; reflect it and ask what importance and confidence look like before moving to advice.
Check feelings explicitly in the agenda (promised at line 3) rather than moving straight to walk counts.
score.summary: Pierre gathered progress, set a drinking goal, and planned for barriers, and used several good complex reflections (lines 19, 22, 30). However, he repeatedly persuaded with judgment and warnings (lines 15, 17, 34, 36), which drew resistance and sustain talk from Tamika.
